# My Journey

I used to preach [Buddhist enlightenment](http://mindset.u-dont-exist.com/) a lot. But an old childhood wound could still hit and suddenly I was the same little kid again, even when the spiritual part of me felt completely free.

The way I picture it is almost stupidly simple. Imagine you're broke and starving, and your baby is starving too. *Understandable*: there is no food. Then a food bank opens nearby and suddenly you've got lots of nutritious munchies. But you're eating all of it yourself while baby you is still starving. *Unforgivable.*

Nobody leaves a baby starving on purpose. I just didn't believe there was a baby. Inner-child stuff sounded silly to me until I could actually feel him. Then reparenting wasn't theoretical anymore. There was a little me there who was hurting, and I could give him some of the love I'd already found.

That also changed how I saw spiritual seeking. I came to think most people who chase spiritual freedom are trying to get above childhood pain, or away from some part of themselves they don't want to meet. That's [spiritual bypassing](https://goenka.u-dont-exist.com/). Plenty of seekers and gurus do it too; I've written about the [Dalai Lama as one example](https://substack.com/@udontexist/note/c-245314772?r=5vdc6m). It doesn't mean people are stupid or crazy. I did it too.

Spending your whole life processing the wounded kid isn't much of an escape either. Spirituality had shown me a much bigger horizon—love and happiness beyond the conditions of my life story. Maybe ordinary life already gives you enough love and meaning. Great. It didn't for me. Conditional love felt radically insufficient, so I kept looking for something deeper.

### Don’t Give the Inner Adult Away

If you still feel like a kid inside, somebody who seems grown-up can feel like salvation. It's easy to hand them the steering wheel. Sometimes that helps. It doesn't make them right about everything.

Even [Pema Chödrön](https://pemachodronfoundation.org/product/taking-the-leap-book/) comes from a tradition where devotion to a teacher is a big deal, and she still says a teacher should “wean us from dependency altogether” and help us grow up.

If your life is actually unsafe, meditation doesn't make it safe. It may change how the pain feels, but sometimes the grown-up job is still to leave or get practical help. Calling real danger merely “your story” leaves the kid there with it.

No-self can also arrive at a terrible time. If you grew up learning that what you wanted didn't matter and you're only just figuring out what you think or learning to say no, “there is no self” can make disappearing easier. Maybe later it feels freeing; first you may need enough of a self to have something to loosen.

If every disagreement gets called “resistance,” the therapist has built a trick where they're right no matter what you say. Maybe they're wrong about you. Maybe the method is going somewhere you don't want to go. They have to be able to consider that.

Borrow adulthood. Do not surrender it.

My own case was weird. I was well-loved as a child, but from age twelve to twenty-six I was depressed and cried every night from feeling the pain of the world. [Loving-kindness (metta) meditation](http://love.u-dont-exist.com/) healed that depression almost instantly for me.

I wasn't lacking love. My parents had given me a lot of it. I found more in [Buddhist teachings—which, it turns out, also include inner-child self-love!](https://substack.com/profile/355021294-u-dont-existcom/note/c-297324975) and later in [loveyhuasca](http://soma.u-dont-exist.com/). Metta gave all that love somewhere to land.

But it didn't reach everything. A lot of the child stuff around my attachment to women was still there. When I later tried [self-directed inner-child therapy](https://youtu.be/yEWFjODXJbI?si=IXUqrhExojOm6Itm), it felt like I was making it up at first. I used San Pedro cactus and CBD tea with sublingual mapacho, and that cracked it open; structured sessions with an inner-child therapist deepened it.

“Find the wounded child and love them” sounded simple until I tried it. A protective part could block me before I even reached the child, and if I did get through I could fall so completely into being the child that the grown-up me disappeared too. Then who was supposed to do the three adult jobs from the map? That problem is why I added borrowed adulthood.
